Answer Batch 0021 mechanically extracted repository-source packet
Deterministic Java validation against quadratic unique-pair oracle
Source-first isolated re-review for the sorted-pair-sum candidate

claims.text: The retained repository source explicitly asks for element pairs in an increasing/sorted array whose sum is 10, and does not preserve output shape, duplicate semantics, index semantics, numeric bounds, or API signature.
Non-decreasing int[] input and returning all unique value pairs are explicit candidate choices rather than recovered source requirements.

For sorted input, a sum below target safely eliminates the current left value, while a sum above target safely eliminates the current right value; equality records a pair and duplicate values may be skipped for unique-value output.
Each pointer moves monotonically across the array, giving O(n) time and O(1) algorithmic auxiliary space excluding O(k) returned pairs.
The implementation casts the left operand to long before addition, preventing int overflow from corrupting target comparison.
The exact Java fixture passes 9 fixed cases and 5000 deterministic randomized sorted arrays against an independent quadratic oracle while confirming no input mutation.
